cards.front: Define the Lebesgue outer measure $m^*$ of a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$.
cards.back: $m^*(A) = \inf\{\sum_{i=1}^\infty (b_i - a_i) : A \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^\infty [a_i, b_i]\}$, where the infimum is over all countable covers by closed intervals.

cards.front: What is the Lebesgue measure of any interval $I = [a,b]$ (or open/half-open variants)?
cards.back: $m(I) = b - a$. This follows because the outer measure equals the length and every interval is measurable.

cards.front: State Carathéodory's criterion for a set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ to be Lebesgue measurable.
cards.back: For every test set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, $m^*(A) = m^*(A \cap E) + m^*(A \cap E^c)$. Sets satisfying this form the Lebesgue $\sigma$-algebra.

cards.front: Prove that Lebesgue measure is countably additive on disjoint measurable sets.
cards.back: Let $\{E_n\}$ be pairwise disjoint measurable sets and $E = \bigcup E_n$. By Carathéodory and induction, $m^*(A) \ge \sum m^*(A \cap E_n) + m^*(A \cap E^c)$ for any $A$; taking $A = E$ yields $m(E) = \sum m(E_n)$.

cards.front: Show that $m^*$ is countably subadditive for arbitrary sets.
cards.back: Given covers of each $A_n$ whose total length sums to within $\varepsilon/2^n$ of $m^*(A_n)$, their union covers $\bigcup A_n$ and has total length $\le \sum m^*(A_n) + \varepsilon$. Hence $m^*(\bigcup A_n) \le \sum m^*(A_n)$.

cards.front: Give an example of a non-Lebesgue-measurable set and the reason it fails measurability.
cards.back: A Vitali set $V \subset [0,1]$ obtained by choosing one representative from each equivalence class modulo $\mathbb{Q}$. The countable disjoint translates $V + q$ ($q \in \mathbb{Q} \cap [-1,1]$) cover $[0,1]$ up to a null set but have identical outer measure; countable additivity would imply $m^*([0,1]) = 0$ or $\infty$, a contradiction.

cards.front: What is a null set in Lebesgue measure theory? Give two examples.
cards.back: Any set $N$ with $m(N) = 0$. Examples: any countable set; the Cantor set (uncountable, measure zero). All subsets of null sets are measurable and null.
